COBALT_PENTEST_ID.description: Server-side Cobalt pentest-scope predicate forwarded as the filter[pentest_id]=<uuid> query parameter on GET /v2/findings. Optional; empty / blank walks the entire org's pentest scope (the typical operational mode for first-time imports). Comma-separated uuids / handles are split and trimmed, then forwarded as multiple filter[pentest_id]=<uuid> entries so a single agent can pull findings from several engagements in one run (e.g. '11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555,acme-mobile-q1'). Cobalt accepts either the pentest uuid or its slug (handle); the operator's COBALT_ORG_TOKEN scope still applies. Whitespace is trimmed around each entry.

COBALT_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional Faraday severity floor (case-insensitive 'info' / 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' / 'critical'); findings whose mapped severity is strictly below the floor are dropped client-side after the fetch. Cobalt's severity label vocabulary is CVSS-aligned ('informational' / 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' / 'critical'); 'informational' / 'none' map to Faraday's 'info' bucket so the finding is still visible. Operator-friendly aliases ('informational' -> 'info', 'moderate' -> 'medium', 'crit' -> 'critical', 'none' -> 'info') are normalised. Closed Cobalt states (invalid / out_of_scope / not_applicable / duplicate / accepted_risk / wont_fix / resolved) are floored to 'info' regardless of the published rating (preserved via an explicit Cobalt-State pivot). Blank / missing / unparseable values keep every record (the typical operational mode for first-time imports).

name: cobalt
title: Cobalt.io
description: Cobalt.io pentest-as-a-service finding importer. Pulls validated findings from the Cobalt.io v2 REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Cobalt.io is a pentest-as-a-service platform — vetted pentesters deliver scoped engagements against the operator's assets and the platform tracks the resulting findings through a triage / acceptance / remediation lifecycle. This executor surfaces validated findings under the operator's existing Faraday workspace so the external pentest pipeline joins the dispatcher's internal scanner output. Endpoints used: GET https://api.cobalt.io/v2/findings?filter[pentest_id]=<uuid>&limit=N&offset=M (paginated pentest finding feed; canonical envelope is JSON:API {'data': [{'id': '...', 'resource': 'Finding', 'attributes': {...}, 'relationships': {...}}], 'links': {'next': '...', 'prev': '...'}, 'meta': {'total': N}} with each record's attributes carrying title, description, log (researcher proof / reproduction notes), type_category (Cobalt's published issue-type ontology — e.g. 'Server Security Misconfiguration', 'Application-Logic & Server-Side', 'Sensitive Data Exposure'), severity ('informational' / 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' / 'critical' — Cobalt's CVSS-aligned ladder), state ('new' / 'triaging' / 'valid_triaged' / 'invalid' / 'out_of_scope' / 'accepted_risk' / 'wont_fix' / 'need_more_info' / 'not_applicable' / 'duplicate' / 'resolved' / 'check_fix' / 'fix_in_progress' — Cobalt's published state machine), affected_targets (list of scoped assets), vulnerable_url (URL the pentester targeted), proof_of_concept / suggested_fix (remediation guidance), cvss_score / cvss_vector, impact / likelihood (Cobalt's 1..5 ladders for the program-set severity rating), created_at / submitted_at / triaged_at / resolved_at / updated_at; relationships carries pointers to pentest (engagement uuid + handle), pentester (researcher username), and asset (scoped target)). The /v2/pentests endpoint is documented for operator reference (the dispatcher never fetches it directly — operators paste the relevant COBALT_PENTEST_ID into the manifest argument). Auth: Cobalt's REST surface uses a long-lived API token in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header plus the organisation-scoped X-Org-Token: <org_token> header (Cobalt's documented v2 auth shape — the API token identifies the user identity, the org token narrows the call to a specific organisation under that identity's access). The dispatcher locks the API version with the Accept: application/vnd.cobalt.v2+json header so later API breaking changes do not silently warp the ingest shape. COBALT_HOST is an env-only override (defaults to https://api.cobalt.io); whitespace is trimmed and https:// is added when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Pagination is offset-based via limit=N + offset=M (Cobalt caps limit at 100); walks until len(records) < page_size or the env-only COBALT_PAGES knob is reached (default 10, clamped to [1, 100]). 401 short-circuits the whole executor (credentials are wrong); 403 / 429 / 5xx stop pagination and return what we have. Each Cobalt finding becomes one Faraday host with host.ip set to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel (pentest findings are keyed on a URL / asset path rather than an IP); the finding title and the vulnerable_url URL land on host.hostnames; the finding itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [PENTEST] engine prefix so external pentester findings land alongside the other crowd-sourced feeds. Severity bucketing: Cobalt's published label vocabulary is 'informational' / 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' / 'critical' (CVSS-aligned); 'informational' / 'none' map to Faraday's 'info' bucket so the finding is still visible. The nested {'rating': '...', 'score': 0..10} shape used by some federated mirrors is tolerated — the rating is preferred and the 0..10 score is used as a fallback (CVSS v3 ranges: 0.0 -> info, 0.1..3.9 -> low, 4.0..6.9 -> medium, 7.0..8.9 -> high, 9.0..10.0 -> critical). Closed Cobalt states (invalid / out_of_scope / not_applicable / duplicate / accepted_risk / wont_fix / resolved) are floored to 'info' regardless of the published rating (preserved via an explicit Cobalt-State pivot). Unparseable / missing severity defaults to 'info'. Status is always 'open' so the operator's remediation workflow takes over; the closed state is preserved via the info-severity floor + the Cobalt-State pivot. Refs include explicit Cobalt-FindingID / Cobalt-Tag / Cobalt-Pentest / Cobalt-Pentester / Cobalt-State / Cobalt-Substate / Cobalt-Type / Cobalt-Severity / Cobalt-CreatedAt / Cobalt-SubmittedAt / Cobalt-TriagedAt / Cobalt-ResolvedAt / Cobalt-UpdatedAt / Cobalt-DisclosedAt / Cobalt-Source / Cobalt-VulnerableURL / Cobalt-CVSSVector / Cobalt-CVSSScore / Cobalt-Impact / Cobalt-Likelihood pivots, plus the canonical https://app.cobalt.io/pentests/<uuid> / https://app.cobalt.io/users/<pentester> / https://app.cobalt.io/findings/<id> permalinks and the canonical NVD CVE + MITRE CWE permalinks for any CVE / CWE ids surfaced in the cve / cwe / type_category / description / title / log fields. Tags: [cobalt, pentest-platforms, finding].
